key_insight: 3D coupled opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 chalcogenide perovskites can deliver very high-efficiency solar cells when thickness, doping, and defects are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for realistic, thermally aware perovskite solar-cell architectures that replace toxic Pb-based absorbers.
method: 3D finite-element COMSOL simulation of a ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 stack
Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer
Systematic optimization of absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF effects
evidence_signal: Optimized simulated devices reached 28.18% PCE for MgZrS3, 26.72% for MgTiS3, and 28.16% for MgHfS3, with corresponding VOC/JSC/FF values reported in the abstract.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based and rely on model assumptions, so experimental validation and real-material interface quality remain key concerns.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
